title: Boss wanted to be CCd on everything
author: Storytime
hook: My new boss told me to CC him on every single email. So I did. Now he's the one being investigated.
story: So my new manager, Derek, started in September. On day one he called me into his office and said he didn't trust my team. From now on, he wanted to be CC'd on every email. Every single one. No exceptions. I asked if he was sure. He said, do I look like I'm joking? So I did exactly what he asked. Client emails. Lunch orders. The printer complaints. Four hundred emails a week. He never said a word. Then three weeks ago, a client sent an urgent email saying our invoice was wrong by forty thousand dollars. I forwarded it to the finance team, and of course, CC'd Derek. Nobody fixed it. The client escalated straight to Derek's boss. And Derek said he was never informed. That's when his boss asked me to search my sent folder. I found the email. Derek was CC'd. Then his boss asked me something else. How many emails had I sent Derek since September? I checked. One thousand nine hundred and twelve. He hadn't opened a single one. Not even the one about his own parking spot. Now HR wants me to send them everything. And Derek is begging me not to. So what do I do?
caption: he said EVERY email. so I sent every email 📧 #storytime
sound: a sneaky, plucky pizzicato sound at very low volume
why: Malicious compliance against a micromanaging boss is a proven revenge theme, the CC rule set up in the first seconds pays off perfectly, and the final question splits the comments.

title: Neighbor left candy with my name
author: Storytime
hook: Every Halloween, my old neighbor left one full size candy bar with my name on it. This year I found out who she really was.
story: When I was six, we moved into a house next to an old lady named Mrs. Hale. She kept to herself. But every Halloween, there was a full size candy bar on her porch with my name on it. Always peanut butter cups. My favorite. I never told her that. I just assumed my mom did. This went on for twenty years. Even after I moved out, the candy bar showed up at my mom's house every October. Last month, Mrs. Hale passed away. A week later, a lawyer called me. Not my mom. Me. Mrs. Hale had left me a box. Inside were photos. Hundreds of them. Me on my first day of school. Me at prom. Me at my college graduation, taken from the back of the crowd. And at the bottom, a letter. It started with, I'm sorry I was never brave enough to tell you. I called my mom and read her the first line. She went completely silent. Then she said, I was going to tell you when you were older. Mrs. Hale wasn't just my neighbor. She was my grandmother. My dad's mother. The dad I was told didn't want me. And the letter explains what really happened. Part two?
caption: twenty years of candy bars and I never knew 🍫 #storytime
sound: a soft, eerie music box melody at very low volume
why: Halloween week hook with a wholesome twist, a small repeated detail (the favorite candy nobody told her about) that becomes the clue, and a strong part two cliffhanger.

title: Mother in law copied my wedding dress
author: Storytime
hook: My mum asked my fiancee for photos of her wedding dress, for the seamstress. We should have asked which seamstress.
story: So my fiancee Clara and I are getting married in December. My mum has always been, let's say, involved. In September she asked Clara for photos of the wedding dress. Every angle. The lace, the back, the buttons. She said a family friend was a seamstress and could help with the fitting. Clara was so happy my mum was finally being nice. Last week, Clara got an email from the bridal shop. It said, thank you for your second order, your gown will be ready in three weeks. Clara never placed a second order. She called the shop. They said a woman came in with photos and ordered the exact same dress. Same lace. Same buttons. Same color. White. The name on the order was my mum's. When I asked her about it, she didn't even deny it. She said it was for a vow renewal with my dad. In the same month. At the same venue. A week after our wedding. Then my dad called me. He had no idea about any vow renewal. So I told my mum she isn't invited until she cancels the order. Now my whole family says I'm destroying the family over a dress. Was I too harsh?
caption: the seamstress was HER 💀 #storytime
sound: a dramatic, suspenseful string sound at very low volume
why: Mother-in-law versus bride is one of the strongest drama themes, the seamstress detail is planted in the hook and pays off in the twist, and the closing question invites strong opinions.
